cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Something in the shared way grates against what you feel. Look at both before you carry it further, and settle it by yourself — one line, to nobody, out loud if you like.
cells.core:
In the shared meaning you keep with people, a standard can outlive its use and you notice, and you don't need a fight to change what gets carried on. New people with new habits don't have to earn a place with you first.

You also know what a clean ending costs, and you don't make anyone pay it twice. When you go to shift something, take one thing the group relies on and weigh it against what it costs the ones who carry it. If it still holds, say so out loud — the rule was doing its job. That's the move you make quietly, done once where the scale can tip.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell what's alive from what's kept out of habit.
cells.verb: composting what a group has outgrown into ground the next meaning can be built on
cells.place: where a shared meaning is carried forward — a standard, a ritual, a story kept alive

cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Someone who shares this meaning with you carries a feeling about it you haven't heard. Put the question plainly, then stay in whatever comes back — no fixing, no steering.
cells.core:
Where you carry a shared meaning, it's being secured ahead of time. The older words are already rising up around you when you walk in — what's being said back, still carried in your own head. Nothing gets to just be lost, and nothing gets to surprise you.

From your side that's care. From the other side it reads like being handed an old part of the story to step into and having to fit it. Live like that for a day: put one plain question to the people who hold this meaning with you — what is it actually like for you — and stay in what comes back without steering it. Not everything needs strengthening before it's begun to wobble.

cells.tense: Back then, something that had run its course was kept standing well past its time.
cells.act: keep the motivation warm with steady care
cells.ask: A practice you help carry — a walk, a call, a meal, something you cook or sing — is nearly out of you. Spend ten minutes on it before the day piles up, nobody told.
cells.core:
Whatever you and whoever holds this with you once made together, the living part of it has thinned. What's kept is the shape — how it's done, when it's done, who stands where — and the reason it's done is somewhere behind where you're standing now. New habits come and go around it and don't reach you.

The want to renew it hasn't gone anywhere in you. It's down one level, under the upkeep. Stay close to what you actually want to do here, and give that the wheel when the motivation comes. Then spend a little on something you keep going — ten minutes, no announcement, before anything else. A small warm thing done for its own sake reminds a practice what it was for, and the wish to hand it on comes with it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the form perfectly while the reason slips behind you.

cells.tense: Right now, decisions about what this group keeps and passes on are being made — one of them yours.
cells.act: set a boundary and hold it
cells.ask: Part of a shared meaning reaches further into you than it should, and you can name it. Say where it ends — once, plainly — and hold that line for a week.
cells.core:
You decide what a group is really carrying. Which parts of an old arrangement stay on for another year, which get set down — someone has to make the call where you live it, and the someone is you. The arrangement holds. Ask who's holding it and the answer is something broad and unowned.

You make the call and it gets filed under custom, or under time. That's why it's tiring without looking like work. One clear line of yours is what will show you how much sway you have: name the part of the shared thing that will only go as far as you allow it to, say it once, and keep it for a week. It doesn't disturb the shared thing; it shows you where your foot has been resting on it.

attempts.check: The record supports the mechanism — right card, right status, right medicine and partner — but the seat is thin: it says shared meaning and tradition, and it does not say which tradition, whose table, or what this person actually keeps alive with anyone. So every cell stays with one group or practice and one ritual or standard carried, never with a culture, a family, a faith or a workplace, and never with what a group feels about them. The ask is a one-time, costless act — one small release, one question, one evening of tending, one line held — so it works even if the person disagrees with my read and would rather keep the arrangement together. The sentence that serves me more than the person is the neater version of the first core: 'what passes through you comes out truer to what it's for' — admiring and vague; I say the plain thing or cut it.
